title: We can't open this 'x-cmdpal' link.
author: blakechartergit
summary: When CmdPal's per-user MSIX deployment or URI registration is blocked, missing, or stale, PowerToys still exposes x-cmdpal activation and produces an opaque 'new app' error instead of reporting package health and remediation.
next_action: Approve package-health detection and actionable CmdPal fallback/error handling.

confidence.rationale: The common missing-registration failure is proven, but several independent deployment policies require different remediation branches.

judgment.rationale: CmdPal's MSIX package or x-cmdpal URI registration fails under several known AppX deployment conditions, but PowerToys continues to expose an activation/settings link that produces an opaque Windows error. PowerToys can detect and explain that state even when enterprise policy itself cannot be bypassed.
evidence: Event Viewer reports AppX failures including 0x80070005, 0x80073CF9, 0x80073CFF, missing VCLibs, and AppLocker blocks.
SYSTEM-context deployment is explicitly rejected for the per-user CmdPal package.
Some machines retain older CmdPal MSIX files and install the wrong version until manually cleaned.
Maintainers proposed checking whether the x-cmdpal URI is registered before invoking it.
Issue #44901 tracks broader unpackaged CmdPal support.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve package-health detection and actionable CmdPal fallback/error handling.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path identified by this lightweight judgment.

proposed_fixes.title: Validate CmdPal package/URI health before exposing activation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: PowerToys assumes the bundled CmdPal MSIX registered successfully and invokes x-cmdpal even when deployment failed, policy blocked the package, dependencies are missing, or a stale payload was selected.
plan: After deployment, verify the expected CmdPal package version and x-cmdpal URI registration for the interactive user.
Select the newest matching package deterministically and record the full AppX deployment error when registration fails.
Disable or replace activation controls with a specific remediation/status message, and link the unpackaged path where enterprise policy prevents MSIX.
verification: Test per-user, per-machine, SYSTEM-context, AppLocker-blocked, sideloading-disabled, missing-dependency, and stale-multiple-MSIX scenarios.
Verify PowerToys never launches an unregistered x-cmdpal URI and always reports the detected package state.

confidence.rationale: The common missing-registration failure is proven, but several independent deployment policies require different remediation branches.

issue_context.summary: When CmdPal's per-user MSIX deployment or URI registration is blocked, missing, or stale, PowerToys still exposes x-cmdpal activation and produces an opaque 'new app' error instead of reporting package health and remediation.
known_information: The failure affects WinGet, Scoop, Chocolatey, EXE, SYSTEM-context, and enterprise-policy environments.
Different reporters supplied precise AppX deployment error codes and dependency/policy details.
Manual installation fixes some machines but is blocked by policy on others.
The problem persists through PowerToys 0.100.2 for enterprise-managed devices.
inferences: There are multiple deployment root causes, but all converge on missing CmdPal package/URI registration.
PowerToys should gate activation/settings controls on package health and preserve the exact AppX error for support.
issue_context.analysis: A single installer change cannot override AppLocker or sideloading policy, but the application can stop invoking an absent URI handler, select the correct package payload, and expose a precise supported/unsupported state.
initial_investigation: Reviewed all 58 live comments, exact AppX errors, install scopes, package-manager cases, workarounds, and related issues.
Verified #44901 remains open as the broader unpackaged CmdPal path; no concrete fix is linked from this issue.

actions.label: Approve CmdPal package-health design
actions.design_summary: Verify package and URI registration, preserve deployment errors, and expose supported remediation
actions.note: Approval starts a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight judgment contains no full design and performs no GitHub write.

actions.label: Reproduce blocked CmdPal registration
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact does not execute the steps or write upstream.

reproduce.version_requirement: Latest stable or Preview PowerToys build
prerequisites: A disposable Windows test account or VM
Ability to test normal user, SYSTEM deployment, or an AppX policy restriction
steps: Install or update PowerToys in the selected deployment context.
Capture the CmdPal AppX deployment result and installed package version.
Open Command Palette settings and invoke activation.
Compare behavior when x-cmdpal is registered versus absent.
reproduce.expected_result: PowerToys detects the exact unsupported or failed package state and never presents the opaque Windows URI-handler dialog.
